title: Strict-local stalk exchange on total-space cohomology
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a local ring homomorphism between strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let $\Lambda$ be any commutative ring, and let $X'\xrightarrow{g'}X$, $X\xrightarrow f\operatorname{Spec}A$, $X'\xrightarrow{f'}\operatorname{Spec}B$ form a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with bottom morphism $g=\operatorname{Spec}(A\to B)$. Let $t$ be the closed geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ defined by its separably closed residue field [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. For every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and every $q\geq0$, there are additive equivalences $a_1:(g^{-1}R^qf_*F)_t\simeq H^q(X,F_{ab})$ and $a_2:(R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F)_t\simeq H^q(X',g'^{-1}F_{ab})$ such that $a_2(\mathrm{Ex}_t(x))=(g')^*(a_1(x))$ for every stalk element $x$. Here the exchange is [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] and the cohomology pullback is [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Neither properness nor torsion nor a closed-fibre comparison is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the module/abelian exchange comparison at the closed B-point to obtain b1,b2 and b2 Ex_module = Ex_abelian b1.
Apply the strict-local abelian comparison to the underlying abelian sheaf, obtaining a1,a2 and a2 Ex_abelian = cohomologyMap a1.
Take the additive equivalences b1.trans a1 and b2.trans a2. For each x, rewrite with the first compatibility and then apply the second compatibility at b1 x.
